notes: inherent: The inherent vowel is said (a rounded a, near o) and typed a, sometimes o (କଥା katha, ଘର ghara / ghar). Odia drops no inherent vowel inside a word in speech, so there is no schwaDeleted list. At the end of a word it is typed or left out (ଓଡ଼ିଶା odisha, ଭୁବନେଶ୍ୱର bhubaneswar), so the skeleton drops a final a. letters: ଯ is j (ଯାଇ jai) and ୟ y (ଭୟ bhaya, ହୋଇଯାଇ); the -ya sign (virama + ଯ) is y (ବ୍ୟବସାୟ byabasaya). ବ is b; the -wa sign ୍ୱ is w or v (ସ୍ୱାମୀ swami). ଶ ଷ ସ are all said s and typed s or sh. ଡ଼ is said r and typed d or r (ଓଡ଼ିଆ odia, ବଡ଼ bada / bara); the tables put the commoner first, and the other spelling reaches the word through the transliterator. ୃ is ru (କୃଷ୍ଣ krushna, ସଂସ୍କୃତି sanskruti) or ri. କ୍ଷ is ksh, khy or x (ଲକ୍ଷ୍ମୀ laxmi), ଜ୍ଞ gy, jn or gn. anusvara: ଂ is n, ng or m (ସଂସ୍କୃତି sanskruti, ଏବଂ ebang / ebam). The skeleton folds ng to n, so ଏବଂ typed ebang finds the word whose key ends in n (calibration skeleton 86.8% to 87.3%); the price is that ଙ୍ଗ words share keys with ନ words. mb and mp fold to nb and np. A final candrabindu ଁ is written or not (ନାହିଁ nahin / nahi), so optionalFinals names it. skeleton: Aspirates fold to their plain letters, sh and chh/ch to s and c, z to j, f to p, v and w to b, q and x to k; aa, ee and oo to a, i and u; ou to au, oi and ae to ai (ଲଗାଇ lagai / lagae), ay to e (Aksharantar's annotators often typed େ as ay: ନେତ୍ରୀ naytri, calibration skeleton 85.2% to 86.8%), ng to n. A final a after a consonant is dropped. apostrophe: An apostrophe marks a dropped vowel (କ'ଣ kana / kan, ତା'ର tar). After a consonant it is spelled by apostropheVowel, as the vowel it stands for; after a vowel sign the walk skips it. The lexicon keeps it in the word.
